item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Nov 3 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Nov 3 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Nov 3 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop — Tue Nov 3, 6:00 PM — Global & International Studies Building
item.description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.
It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.
Instructions:
Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session
If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop.
If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.
A

item.title: Jubilee Event — Tue Nov 3, 6:00 PM — BLGA 1050 Global Lounge - Global & International Studies
item.description:
It’s a discussion activity where a statement is presented. People stand on a line based on how much they agree or disagree with a statement. After choosing a spot, participants explain why they chose their position and listen to different perspectives. They can even move if their opinion changes. The goal is to have a great conversation and understand why people think the way they do. The event is all about having real conversations about what creates change in Black communities. Participants will respond to different statements and share their opinions on topics like activism, voting, economic empowerment, leadership, and community involvement. The goal is to hear different perspectives, learn from one another, and have an open discussion about the many ways people believe progress happens.
Hosted by: Black Men Evolve
Online Location: https://imu.indiana.edu/event-planning/spaces/frangipani-room.html
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12

item.title: Ostrom Workshop | Research Series: Xinyi Zhao — Wed Nov 4, 1:00 PM — The Ostrom Workshop
item.description: Bio Xinyi Zhao is a PhD student in Anthropology at Indiana University Bloomington. Her research focuses on collective action, disaster response, and state-society relations in contemporary China. Her dissertation examines the 2021 Henan flood, with particular attention to how volunteer rescue organizations, local communities, and other civil actors mobilized and coordinated during the disaster. Building on ethnographic fieldwork in urban and rural Henan, her research explores how collective action emerges under conditions of uncertainty and how it is shaped by uneven landscapes, infrastructures, and relations with the state. Her broader interests include political anthropology, environmental anthropology, infrastructure, and disaster.Title Collective Action and Institutional Emergence in Urban China's Climate DisastersAbstract This paper examines how spontaneous collective action and subsequent institution-building emerge during climate disasters under China's authoritarian urban go

item.title: Art That Changed Me: One Image, One Story — Thu Nov 5, 4:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Art can be anything that inspires us—a painting, a building, a fashion collection, a photograph, a piece of music, a place, or even an everyday object that changes the way we see the world. In collaboration with the Art Therapy Program at the Eskenazi Museum, Art That Changed Me invites attendees to share one image (physical or digital) and one story about something that has inspired, challenged, or shaped who they are. Through brief 3–5 minute presentations, participants will celebrate the diverse experiences, passions, and creative journeys that make up our community while exploring the powerful connections between creativity, reflection, and wellbeing. Participants are encouraged to bring their content ready to go on a flash drive to enable ease of loading in for their presentations quickly.
Source: Architecture + Design, Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Eskenazi School of Art

item.title: Vaulted Treasures — Fri Nov 6 — Brown County Art Guild
item.description:
Vaulted Treasures offers a rare opportunity to rediscover the Guild’s historic collection through a selection of works that have never before been framed or have not been exhibited in recent years. Featuring landscapes, still lifes, and portraits by the Guild’s founders, the exhibition reveals both familiar and lesser-seen treasures from the Guild’s artistic legacy. Several historic works are presented in new frames made possible through a grant from the Brown County Community Foundation, offering these pieces a renewed presence for contemporary audiences.
Source: Brown County Art Guild

item.title: Sounds From the Black Hole featuring Tim Kaiser — Fri Nov 6, 8:45 PM — Allison-Jukebox Community Center
item.description:
Tim Kaiser returns to Bloomington, "taking a hammer to melody and rhythm and pounding them into texture." Tim is the Dr. Frankenstein of noise, resurrecting retired bodies with new circuitry, inciting new resonances within them. Artifacts of the past become the music of the future. If you are curious and in search of sound yourself, you may even be able to go home with a piece of his work.
The Black Hole House Band is expanding to a possible sextet (or beyond!) with faces both familiar and new, plus special guests Justin Clifford Rhody and Abigail Smith, former Bloomingtonians living now in New Mexico. The House Band will play an early and a late set.
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Nov 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Nov 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Nov 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery.
